cohort: The cohort consisted of 181 pregnant women, comprising 109 cases with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) and 72 controls with pregnancies scheduled for induction or elective cesarean section between 37 and 40 weeks of gestation.
finding: The fetal TEI index was significantly increased in pregnancies complicated by intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP), correlated with bile acid levels, and significantly reduced after ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) administration.
cross-section timing: Measurements were performed during pregnancy, with a median gestational age at inclusion of 35.9 weeks for ICP cases and between 37-40 weeks for controls.
gest_age: Median 35.9 weeks (IQR, 33.0-38.9) for ICP cases; 37-40 weeks for controls
